summary: Douglas Co., OR site in the Umpqua NF: crow's nest c.1920, D-6 cupola cabin 1928, staffed into the 1960s; cabin moved to Tiller Ranger Station in 1985 and displayed there.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin that replaced an earlier crow's nest in a tree
facts.status_note: Cabin moved to the Tiller Ranger Station in 1985 and is described as on display there. No source describes the Red Mountain site today.

staffing.status: Staffed into the 1960s per NHLR; named lookouts in newspaper items from the 1920s and early 1930s

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

access.note: The cabin is an historic exhibit at the Tiller Ranger Station per NHLR, and the Weebly history says it is on display there. The sources give no opening hours, and we did not check the site.

events.note: Crow's nest set up on the summit about 1920 (FFLOS); NHLR calls it a tree tower built by the Umpqua National Forest in about 1920.
A June 1922 newspaper item describes Mr. and Mrs. Looney at the station; the earliest staffing item we found.
George Newman placed in the lookout station temporarily during a dry spell (November 1925).
D-6 cupola cabin replaced the crow's nest. An August 1929 item describes progress on the new lookout house, so the build year is not settled (see resolved_conflicts).
February 1930 item: H. P. Looney has received his commission for the 1930 season; a standard lookout house had replaced the tent once used.
Cabin moved to the Tiller Ranger Station as a display.
NHLR says the cabin has been restored as an historic exhibit after its 1985 move. No separate restoration year is given.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as US 896, OR 263 on March 28, 2011.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 911, OR 116 on August 16, 2011.

corrections.current: None relocated (The lookout was moved to Tiller Ranger.)
corrections.proposed: Cabin moved to the Tiller Ranger Station in 1985 and displayed there.
corrections.why: The brief's event text says 'None relocated' and then describes the 1985 move. All sources agree on the move, so the 'None relocated' wording is wrong.

resolved_conflicts.field: build year of the D-6 cupola cabin
resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS, NHLR and Firelookout give 1928. An August 1929 newspaper item describes progress on the new lookout house. The story says the sources do not settle the year.
The FFLOS site record (US 896) and the NHLR tower record (US 911) give different coordinates. The sources do not explain the gap, and the story does not use coordinates.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 'None relocated' event wording is corrected above. The NHLR record (US 911) and the FFLOS site record (US 896) are separate registrations for the same lookout; the story uses both. Staffing names after 1930 were not found beyond 'staffed into the 1960s'. The Tiller Historical Trail page on the Forest Service site (recid 63864) appeared in a search result, but the cached page was a recreation listing that did not include the lookout description, so it is not cited. Opening hours and current access were not confirmed. Budget note: this tower went over the six-page-read budget (about 9 fetches including repeats) and used no WebSearch.
